references.text: Deals with removing the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, the same theme of avoiding bloodguilt in the land
Continues the theme of innocent blood and Israel's responsibility to cleanse the land from bloodguilt
Explains that blood defiles the land, and that the land cannot be cleansed except by the blood of the one who shed it
The establishment of cities of refuge in the promised land to protect against blood vengeance
Reference to innocent blood in Judah which the Lord would not forgive
Jeremiah warns against bringing innocent blood upon the people by judging them unjustly
Judas' confession that he has betrayed innocent blood, echoing the Old Testament principle
